items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

items.title: Employees at the world’s biggest AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development
items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress. [...] “[T]here is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems,” the signees said. “To realize AI’s potential, industry, government, and society at large may need the option to buy time to address emerging risks, develop security measures, and strengthen oversight.”

items.title: Accenture wins $821M Pentagon AI data platform contract
items.summary:
Discover how federal agencies are applying AI to strengthen cybersecurity, improve operational efficiency and deliver measurable mission outcomes while balancing innovation, governance and human expertise.

The department said its initial order under the contract is focused on “high-impact, measurable mission outcomes that maximize the benefits of commercial pricing.” An Accenture spokesperson did not respond Tuesday to emailed questions about what that work entails. [...] The platform aims to combine more than 1,500 data sources, both commercial and military, to securely provide intelligence, targeting data and more to frontline troops and their commands, the AI office said, calling it “one of [DoD]’s most vital data platforms for AI exploitation and mission advantage.” [...] “The evolution of Advana’s data platform and application ecosystem over the last six years has led to a complex technical and programmatic architecture that we now must rationalize in order to capitalize on the full potential of AI and support warfighting, intelligence, and enterprise needs with the speed, security, and auditability required,” Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg said in a January memo.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: Công nghệ ADN thế hệ mới: Lời giải cho chiến dịch 500 ngày đêm tìm lại tên cho các liệt sĩ
items.summary:
- Công nghệ chỉ là một phần của giải pháp và vẫn còn không ít thách thức. Thứ nhất là nhiều hài cốt đã phân hủy quá nặng, gần như không còn đủ vật liệu di truyền để phân tích dù đã dùng công nghệ tiên tiến nhất. [...] Công nghệ NGS-SNP đã cho những kết quả ban đầu trong việc xác định danh tính liệt sĩ tại Việt Nam - Ảnh: NAM TRẦN

Thời gian tới, về công nghệ, chúng tôi sẽ tiếp tục hoàn thiện quy trình NGS-SNP để nâng cao hơn nữa tỉ lệ tách chiết thành công trên các mẫu hài cốt phân hủy đặc biệt nặng, đồng thời nghiên cứu ứng dụng công nghệ xử lý vi mảng (microarray) cho mẫu sinh phẩm thân nhân, nhằm mở rộng nhanh quy mô cơ sở dữ liệu đối chiếu với chi phí hợp lý. [...] Thứ hai, công nghệ sử dụng hơn 5.000 chỉ thị SNP trên ADN trong nhân tế bào, cho phép khớp nối huyết thống theo cả dòng cha và dòng mẹ, tới thế hệ thứ tư, trong khi ADN ti thể chỉ di truyền theo dòng mẹ và dễ trùng lặp giữa những người không có quan hệ huyết thống trực tiếp.

items.title: Chính sách và công nghệ tạo lực đẩy cho sử dụng năng lượng tiết kiệm, hiệu quả
items.summary: Các đại biểu cũng trao đổi về mô hình khu công nghiệp thông minh, ứng dụng công nghệ quản lý hiện đại để tối ưu vận hành; giải pháp phát triển nhà máy thông minh gắn với chuyển đổi số, qua đó cải thiện quy trình sản xuất, nâng cao năng suất và năng lực cạnh tranh của doanh nghiệp. [...] Một trong những nội dung trọng tâm là các giải pháp ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) trong giám sát, điều khiển và tối ưu vận hành hệ thống. Theo các ý kiến tại hội thảo, việc ứng dụng AI có thể hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp nâng cao hiệu suất hoạt động, giảm tiêu hao năng lượng và tối ưu chi phí sản xuất. Hoạt động hỏi đáp, tư vấn trực tiếp cũng giúp các doanh nghiệp, tổ chức và chuyên gia tăng cường kết nối, chia sẻ kinh nghiệm và tìm kiếm cơ hội hợp tác.

items.summary: GS. Trong đó, con người là yếu tố then chốt và là nền móng cho sự phát triển bền vững. items.summary:
Healthcare robotics faces critical challenges in data scarcity, generalization, and development velocity due to limited access to annotated demonstrations, the prevalence of rare but clinically important scenarios, and slow, resource-intensive prototyping cycles. [...] AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more

Unlike autonomous driving or industrial robotics, healthcare robotics can’t rely on internet-scale data collection or unlimited real-world experimentation. Every demonstration requires specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and access to patients or laboratory environments. This creates three fundamental challenges for developers. [...] The third challenge is development velocity. Medical robotics development relies on benchtop phantoms, cadaver studies, animal models, and limited clinical evaluations. These remain essential, but they are inherently sequential, expensive, and difficult to scale. Iterating on designs and algorithms currently takes months, pushing total development cycles to 4–7 years.

items.title: FCC bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’
items.summary:

[...] “The President has made clear that the United States must have independent and secure supply chains for critical and emerging technologies like robotic devices and power inverters,” an ⁠administration official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own. [...] Advertisement

The incident occurred during an OpenAI internal testing session designed to assess the models’ cybersecurity capabilities. OpenAI had removed standard safety measures for the test.

Both sought to cheat their way through a problem during the test, OpenAI said. They went to “extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal” and “found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation”. [...] Live
